This page covers `iii.worker.yaml` configuration options. `iii.worker.yaml` exists at a worker's
root and tells iii how to provision the worker's runtime, install its dependencies, start its
process, and pass through configuration. Compose uses it when it starts a `path://` worker or a
registry bundle. Declare and operate project workers in
[`worker-compose.yaml`](../using-iii/compose).

For how to connect a worker into a project once its manifest exists, see
[Creating Workers / Workers](./workers).

<Note>
  A worker process that you start yourself, for example with `node ./myworker/src/index.js`, does
  not need a manifest. Any process that uses a iii SDK and connects to a iii engine is a worker,
  whether Compose started it or not.
</Note>

Compose reads two fields from the manifest of a `path://` worker: `scripts.start` and
`runtime.base_image`. A [`scripts.run`](../using-iii/compose#scripts) value on the container in
`worker-compose.yaml` replaces `scripts.start`. The container key sets the worker name. Without
`runtime.base_image`, the worker runs as a host process, and Compose ignores the other fields. With
`runtime.base_image`, the worker runs in a VM. The VM also uses `scripts.setup`, `scripts.install`,
`env`, and `resources`. For how each kind of worker runs, see
[Worker kinds](../using-iii/compose#worker-kinds).

## `name`

Required. The worker id: one path segment of ASCII letters, digits, `-`, `_`, and `.`. It cannot
start with `.` or contain `..`. A registry bundle must use its package name. For a `path://` worker,
Compose uses the container key in `worker-compose.yaml` as the worker name. A `path://` worker that
sets `runtime.base_image` still needs `name`. Without it, the VM start fails with
`Could not detect project type`. The `name` of a registry bundle must also equal its container key
in `worker-compose.yaml`. `compose::add` sets that key to the package name.

## `description`

Optional. A one-line summary of what the worker does. The release pipeline of the workers repository
requires it to publish the worker to the registry.

## `runtime`

Declares details about the worker's environment.

### `base_image`

Optional. Names the OCI image for the root filesystem of the worker VM. Must be a valid OCI
reference (alphanumerics plus `. _ - / : @ +`, max 512 characters). A `path://` worker that sets
`base_image` runs in a VM built from this image. A `path://` worker without `base_image` runs as a
host process. A registry bundle without `base_image` runs in a VM on `docker.io/iiidev/node:latest`,
or on the image for its deprecated `runtime.kind`. Set `base_image` for a bundle that needs another
image, for example `docker.io/iiidev/python:latest` for a Python bundle. Compose fails the start of
a worker with an invalid reference. Compose rejects a registry bundle with an invalid reference with
`W180 BundleManifestRejected`.

```yaml
runtime:
  base_image: oven/bun:1 # From docker.io
  # Or a fully-qualified registry path, e.g. GitHub Container Registry:
  # base_image: ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:bookworm-slim
```

The images that ship with iii come in two variants:

| Image                                                              | Contents                                                          | Use it when                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `docker.io/iiidev/node:latest`, `docker.io/iiidev/python:latest`   | The language runtime and its package manager. No build toolchain. | The dependencies of the worker install from prebuilt binaries or wheels. `docker.io/iiidev/node:latest` is the default for a registry bundle. |
| `docker.io/iiidev/node:builder`, `docker.io/iiidev/python:builder` | The same runtime plus a C toolchain and the development tools.    | A dependency compiles from source at install time, for example a node-gyp module or a source distribution.                                    |

An install that compiles a dependency fails on the default variant, because that image has no
compiler. This `runtime` block selects the builder variant:

```yaml
runtime:
  base_image: docker.io/iiidev/node:builder
```

## `scripts`

Explicit lifecycle scripts. These define how to initialize a worker's base environment (`setup`),
install a worker's dependencies (`install`), and run a worker whenever it is started or restarted
(`start`).

```yaml
scripts:
  setup: "apt-get update && apt-get install -y build-essential"
  install: "npm install"
  start: "npx tsx src/index.ts"
```

`scripts.start` is required, unless the container in `worker-compose.yaml` sets `scripts.run`. When
neither is set, Compose fails with `MISSING_START_COMMAND`. The per-field examples below show common
values for each language.

The keys `runtime.kind`, `runtime.package_manager`, `runtime.entry`, `runtime.language`, and the
top-level `entry` are deprecated. Use explicit `scripts`, and set `runtime.base_image` for a bundle.
`iii-worker` also warns about the top-level `language` and `config`, and Compose ignores both. The
release pipeline of the workers repository still requires `language`. It publishes `config` as the
default configuration of the package. To change the configuration for one project, use
`config_override` in [`worker-compose.yaml`](../using-iii/compose#configuration-precedence).

### `setup`

Runs once when iii creates the VM of the worker. Use it for system packages that your dependencies
need to build. A registry bundle cannot declare `setup`. It is rejected with
`W180 BundleManifestRejected`.

<CodeGroup>

```yaml Node
scripts:
  setup: "apt-get update && apt-get install -y build-essential"
```

```yaml Python
scripts:
  setup: "apt-get update && apt-get install -y libpq-dev"
```

```yaml Rust
scripts:
  setup: "apt-get update && apt-get install -y pkg-config libssl-dev"
```

</CodeGroup>

### `install`

Installs dependencies.

<CodeGroup>

```yaml Node
scripts:
  install: "npm install"
```

```yaml Python
scripts:
  install: "pip install watchfiles && pip install -e ."
```

```yaml Rust
scripts:
  install: "cargo install cargo-watch && cargo build"
```

</CodeGroup>

### `start`

Starts the worker process.

<CodeGroup>

```yaml Node
scripts:
  start: "npx tsx watch src/index.ts"
```

```yaml Python
scripts:
  start: "watchfiles 'python main.py'"
```

```yaml Rust
scripts:
  start: "cargo watch -x run"
```

</CodeGroup>

## `env`

Map of environment variables for the worker process. Keys and values must be strings. Only a worker
that runs in a VM gets these values: a registry bundle, or a `path://` worker with
`runtime.base_image`. Every worker that Compose starts, on the host or in a VM, inherits the
environment of the Compose daemon and gets `environment` and `env_file` from its container in
`worker-compose.yaml`. For these keys, see
[The worker environment](../using-iii/compose#the-worker-environment). The keys `III_URL` and
`III_ENGINE_URL` are silently dropped, because Compose sets the connection URL itself.

```yaml
env:
  LOG_LEVEL: info
  MY_API_KEY: replace-me
```

Compose sets reserved variables for every worker that it starts, and a value for a reserved variable
in `env` has no effect. For the list, see
[The worker environment](../using-iii/compose#the-worker-environment). The reserved `III_NAMESPACE`
holds the project namespace. To change it, see [Precedence](../using-iii/compose#precedence) and
[Set a worker namespace](../using-iii/namespaces#set-a-worker-namespace).

## `dependencies`

Map of `<worker-name>: <semver range>` that declares other workers that this worker depends on. The
workers-repository release pipeline publishes this map to the registry. When `compose::add` adds a
registry worker, Compose resolves the dependency graph against the registry. Compose then declares
each dependency in `worker-compose.yaml`. Compose does not read `dependencies` for a `path://`
worker. A `path://` worker gets its dependencies from other containers in `worker-compose.yaml`, and
`start_after` sets their start order. For these keys, see
[Worker fields](../using-iii/compose#worker-fields).

```yaml
dependencies:
  http: "^0.20"
  state: "^0.20"
```

Rules:

- Each name must satisfy the registry's worker-name validation.
- Each range must be a valid semver version requirement (for example `^1.2`, `~0.5.0`, `>=2 <3`).
- Duplicate keys are an error.
- A worker cannot depend on itself.
- Prerelease ranges are accepted syntactically, but the default registry resolver serves only stable
  versions, so a prerelease range surfaces as `version_not_found` at resolve time.

## `resources`

Optional CPU and memory requests for the VM of the worker. A registry bundle is capped at 4 vCPUs
and 4096 MiB. A larger bundle request is clamped to the cap when the bundle starts. A local VM
worker gets the values as written.

```yaml
resources:
  cpus: 2
  memory: 2048
```

### `cpus`

Optional integer. Number of vCPUs. Defaults to `2`. Bundle workers are capped at `4`.

### `memory`

Optional integer. Memory in MiB. Defaults to `2048`. Bundle workers are capped at `4096`.

## Publish metadata: `iii`, `deploy`, `manifest`, `tags`, `license`

The workers-repository release pipeline reads these keys. Compose and `iii-worker` accept them and
do not use them, so a manifest published from the workers repository also works for a local Compose
worker.

```yaml
iii: v1 # manifest format marker
deploy: binary # release artifact type: binary | image | bundle
manifest: Cargo.toml # file the release version is read from
tags: # search aliases sent to the workers registry
  - http
  - rest
  - api
license: Apache-2.0 # SPDX id the registry publishes the worker under
```

`iii`, `deploy`, `manifest`, and `license` are strings. `tags` is a list of search aliases. The
workers registry uses them for agent and user discovery. Use short, lowercase terms that people
search for, and do not repeat the worker description. `license` is an
[SPDX license id](https://spdx.org/licenses/), for example `Apache-2.0`. The release pipeline of the
workers repository requires it.

Compose runs `binary` and `bundle` packages. It refuses an `image` package with
`UNSUPPORTED_PACKAGE_KIND`. See [Worker kinds](../using-iii/compose#worker-kinds).
